preconditions.description: The number of words in Old Berland language is between 1 and 1000, inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= li <= 1000 for li in lengths)
preconditions.description: The lengths of the words are natural numbers not exceeding 1000.

postconditions.description: The output is either 'YES' or 'NO' indicating whether the words can be reconstructed.

postconditions.expression: output == 'YES' ==> (len(words) == N and all(isinstance(word, str) and len(word) == len(words[0]) for word in words))
postconditions.description: If the output is 'YES', then there are exactly N words of the same length, and each word consists of the characters '0' and '1'.
If the output is 'NO', then no words can be reconstructed.
